No. S. B. D. 8200/45
Date 8 / 8 / 40

August 7, 40.

Dear Mr. Tyrrell,

In reply to your letter of August 6, I
outline hereinafter the circumstances surrounding
the seizure of Chinese textbooks from the premises
of the World Book Company on June 11.

Representatives of M.I.J.M. Gendarmerie
complained of anti-Japanese propaganda contained in
textbooks entitled "New Common Knowledge for Junior
Primary School, No. 7" and "Mandarin Reader for
High Primary School". The book store was visited
and copies of the offending books were examined. It
was decided that the books ought not, during the
present tense situation, be exhibited for sale. A
number of copies were seized and brought to Special
Branch. Subsequently a complaint was made to the
Council by the World Book Company through the medium
of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce. The matter was
amicably settled as related to you verbally.

Yours sincerely,

R.W.C.

G. F. Tyrrell, Esq.,
H.B.M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

6th August, 1940.

Personal.

Dear Mr. Yorke,

We have received through the Embassy a memorandum from the Wai Chiao-pu in which it is stated that on the 11th June a number of Chinese and Foreign detectives of the Central Police Station, during a search of the Sales Department of the World Book Company, (the address of which is given in the current hong list as No. 390 Foochow Road), took away all the copies stored there of the Higher Primary School National Language, Book 3, edited by Chu I Hsin ( 朱 毅 新 ) and the Lower Primary School Common Knowledge, Book 7, edited by Tung Wen ( 董 文 ). The memorandum continues that these books have not, so far, been returned, though the Company have made representations to the Municipal Council. I imagine that these books were seized by you because they contained undesirable material, but I shall be grateful for any more precise information which you can give me.

Yours sincerely,

        Mr. Loh's letter of June 18, 1940, raises questions
which, I submit, ought not to be raised by broadminded Chinese
citizens at the present time owing to the political situation.
Dealing with the letter by paragraphs :-
1. It cannot be denied that the Central Government did approve

    face the local situation as it is and not as recorded in

    control of the schools in the Settlement and in fact has
    obtained control of many schools. It is quite possible that
    further seizures of text books will have to be made but not
    if local school authorities will delete certain texts deemed
    to be offensive by the local Chinese ruling authorities
    and their supporters.
4. It is not denied that the text books are the property of the
    World Book Co. but as the books offend against the Council's
    proclamation and notification, they are subject to seizure.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 25 JUN 1940）

G. G. Phillips, Esq.,
Commissioner & Secretary General,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir:

We beg to acknowledge receipt of your reply, No. A 1/10
dated June 14, 1940, regarding to the seizure of our school
textbooks which are regarded as unsuitable for sale in the
Settlement under existing condition.

We wish that you will reconsider this matter for the
following reasons:

(1) These textbooks were all published according to
the regulations of the Central Government. The matters there-
by contained were all approved by the Ministry of Education, and we,
the publishers, are not allowed to make any changes
as soon as the textbook is published and registered. Now, if
there is anything considered as objectionable, it is beyond
our power to make any re-adjustment, unless the Council will
go through the proper diplomatic channels to ask the Government
for changes.

(2) We do not know yet what the nature of the objec-
tionable matter is in these textbooks. If it is an historical
fact, then it is impossible for any one to make changes, and
if a person should be blamed in such a case, it is not the one
who told the story but the one who did the fact. It is not
wise to cheat ourselves as to close up the fact which has
really long been disclosed to the world. We hope that it is
not the case that we would have to re-write the history.

(3) We are afraid that the present case will set up
a bad precedent for certain people to take advantages, as it
has long been rumoured that they are trying to get control
of the schools in the Settlement. It is possible that all
textbooks not only from our company but also from the other
publishers might be seized by the same way in the future.
If so, then there will be no textbooks available for the
schools in the Settlement. How can a school carry on without
textbooks? It must be a serious question.

(4) Although these textbooks are regarded as unsuit-
able for sale, yet they are our property. We have right to
claim for possession. They can not be seized or confiscated,
since we have not done anything wrong in so far.

For these reasons and the reasons stated in our pre-
vious letter, you are, therefore, requested to consider this
matter again and instruct the Central Police Station to return
us these textbooks as soon as possible.

Thanking you in anticipation, we remain,

Faithfully yours

THE WORLD BOOK CO., LTD.
K. I. Loh
General Manager.

尊敬的先生：

谨确认收到您1940年6月14日关于查扣我校教科书的回复（编号 A 1/10），这些教科书被认为在现有条件下不适合在租界内销售。

出于以下原因，我们希望您重新考虑此事：

(1) 这些教科书均按照中央政府的规定出版。其中包含的内容均经教育部批准，且一旦教科书出版并注册，我们作为出版商不得做任何更改。现在，如果有任何内容被视为不妥，这超出了我们的调整能力，除非工部局通过适当的外交渠道要求政府进行更改。

(2) 我们尚不清楚这些教科书中不妥内容的性质。如果是历史事实，那么任何人都不可能做出更改，如果在这种情况下有人应受指责，那也不是讲述故事的人，而是制造事实的人。自欺欺人地掩盖早已向世界公开的事实是不明智的。我们希望情况并非如此，即我们不得不重写历史。

(3) 我们担心本案会为某些人利用开创不良先例，因为早有谣言称他们正试图控制租界内的学校。未来，不仅我们公司的教科书，其他出版商的教科书也可能以同样方式被查扣。如果是这样，租界内的学校将无教科书可用。学校若无教科书如何运作？这必然是一个严重的问题。

(4) 虽然这些教科书被认为不适合销售，但它们仍是我们的财产。我们有权主张占有权。它们不能被查扣或没收，因为迄今为止我们并未做任何错事。

基于上述理由以及我们前一封信中陈述的理由，特此请求您再次考虑此事，并指令中央捕房尽快将这些教科书归还我方。

提前致谢，此致

忠实于您的

世界书局有限公司
K. I. Loh

June 12, 1940.

Seizure of alleged anti-Japanese Chinese language
text books.

At 3 p.m. June 11th, Lieutenant Kotoda and
Corporal Morishita of the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters, Bridge House, North Szechuen Road,
applied to Special Branch for assistance in seizing
copies of two text books in the Chinese language
entitled "New Common Knowledge for Junior Primary
School" No. 7 and "Mandarin Reader for High Primary
School" which they stated contained anti-Japanese
lessons.

Acting on the instructions of D.C. (Special
Branch), D.S.I. MacAdie, D.S. Kamashita, C.A. Loh Sih-
Kya, C.D.S. 24 and C.D.C. 281 at 3.30 p.m., in company
with the members of the Japanese military above
mentioned, visited the World Book Company (世界書局),
390 Foochow Road, publishers of the text books in
question. The Sales Manager Lieu Chi-kang (劉季康)
was interviewed and was advised to produce all copies
of the books described. Accordingly, 1,712 copies of the
book "New Common Knowledge" and 1,003 copies of the
"Mandarin Reader" were handed over and taken to Special
Branch together with the Sales Manager.

According to the manager, 3,000 copies of the
first named publication and 2,000 copies of the second
named publication had been printed by the World Book
Company and with the exception of these seized, the
remainder had all been sold over the counter locally.

A statement was taken from the Sales Manager
which is attached together with translations of the
extracts from the books to which exception is taken by
the Japanese military.

The Sales Manager was allowed to leave at 4.30 p.m.
same day.

根据政治部助理处长的指示，麦阿迪（MacAdie）副督察、龟下（Kamashita）副督察、华捕探目陆锡嘉（Loh Sih-Kya）、华捕探长24号及华捕探目281号于下午3时30分，在上述日本军方人员陪同下，前往福州路390号世界书局，即涉案教科书的出版商。警方接见了营业部主任刘季康，并告知其交出所述书籍的所有副本。据此，1712册《新常识》及1003册《国语读本》被移交并连同营业部主任一起带往政治部。

FULL PARTICULARS OF TAIWAN'S RESISTANCE AGAINST JAPAN

Eighteen years prior to the inauguration of the
Chinese Republic, a war broke out between China and Japan.
China was defeated and the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed.
China suffered heavy losses.

Taiwan was ceded to Japan, as stipulated in the
Treaty of Shimonoseki. Upon learning of this, the
inhabitants of Taiwan became indignant. One Chu San-kung
(丘仙根) was so angry that he promoted a Righteous and
Brave Corps to resist the Japanese. Several tens of
thousands of persons voluntarily joined him in a few days.
They took oath to oppose the Japanese administration. They
requested Governor Tong Ching-soong (唐景崧) (to be the
President of the Righteous and Brave Corps and to take charge
of anti-Japanese military affairs. In view of the enthusiasm
of the people, Governor Tong converted the Governor's Yamen
in Tai-pei into a Presidential Office, and immediately started
the training of troops, the raising of funds and the procuring
of provisions in preparation for a life-and-death struggle
with the Japanese.

Japanese warships arrived and troops were landed.
The Japanese troops headed straight for Keelung (基隆),
Much disturbance was created by them. The inhabitants of
Taiwan would be killed should they put up even a little
resistance. General Wu Kwoh-hwa (吳國華) bravely
attacked the brutal Japanese soldiers and won a great victory.
The Japanese soldiers fled back to their ships.

Unfortunately, the lower grade officers under
General Wu fought for merit with the result that the defenders

台湾抗日实录

中华民国成立前十八年，中日之间爆发了一场战争。中国战败，签署了《马关条约》。中国遭受了重大损失。

根据《马关条约》规定，台湾被割让给日本。得知此事后，台湾居民义愤填膺。有一位丘仙根（Chu San-kung）愤而发起义勇军抵抗日军。数万人在几天内自愿加入。他们宣誓反对日本统治。他们请求巡抚唐景崧（Tong Ching-soong）担任义勇军总统并负责抗日军事。鉴于民众的热情，唐巡抚将台北的巡抚衙门改为总统府，并立即开始训练军队、筹集资金和采购粮食，准备与日军进行殊死搏斗。

日本军舰抵达，部队登陆。日军直扑基隆，制造了巨大的骚乱。台湾居民稍有抵抗即遭杀戮。吴国华（Wu Kwoh-hwa）将军英勇攻击残暴的日军并赢得大捷。日军逃回舰上。

不幸的是，吴将军麾下的下级军官争功，导致守军

became careless. The Japanese troops took advantage of this
and launched an attack. The situation in Keelung became
serious. General Liu encouraged the soldiers to attack the
Japanese soldiers and at the same time, he asked for
assistance from the President of the Righteous and Brave Corps.
Reenforcements were immediately sent by Tong
Ching-soong. Unexpectedly, the officers commanding the
reenforcements became afraid when they learned that there
were many Japanese soldiers. They hesitated and Keelung
was captured by the Japanese.
Keelung is the gateway to Taiwan. No other
strategic position was left. Though the people might unite
it was not easy to resist the Japanese. Furthermore, due
to divergence of views, disturbances arose among the
Chinese, and the Japanese troops found they could advance
easily.
In view of the critical situation, Tong Ching-soong
realized that it would be impossible to do anything. He mingled
with the refugees and escaped in disguise. The situation
became worse after the desertion of Tong Ching-soong. Chu
San-kung gathered all the members of the Righteous and Brave
Corps in the vicinity and prepared for a life-and-death
struggle with the Japanese. Before preparations could be
completed, the Japanese troops had reached the city wall.
At that moment, a general named Liu Yung-foh
(刘永福) still held positions in Tai-nan, and swore to
resist the Japanese until death. Fierce attacks were
launched by the Japanese troops, but they failed to defeat
him. An encircling movement was carried out lasting
several months but without success. Finally, due to
shortage of provisions among the Chinese, the Japanese troops

变得疏忽大意。日军趁机发动进攻。基隆局势变得严峻。刘将军鼓励士兵攻击日军，同时向义勇军总统请求援助。唐景崧立即派出增援部队。出乎意料的是，指挥增援部队的军官得知日军众多后心生畏惧。他们犹豫不决，导致基隆被日军占领。

2 JUN

The World Book Company, Ltd.,
290 Foochow Road,
Shanghai, China, June 11, 1940.

C.F. Phillips, Esq.,
Commissioner & Secretary General,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir:

We regret to report that your policemen with some Japanese in plain clothing searched our Sales Department at No. 290 Foochow Road at three o'clock in the afternoon, June 11, 1940, and took away about one thousand copies of the primary school textbooks which were all published before the war, approved and registered in the very Government that your Government has so long recognized.

As a ratepayer, we must complain that such an action not only disturbs our business alone but also affects the spirit of co-operation with the Council in general. We recall that in the past we used to have a mutual understanding that if there is a book which is not so fit to the present situation, the Police Office will notify us and we will do accordingly. So, we have enjoyed our fine co-operation and have not met any troubles whatever. But it is now changed all of sudden. The action was taken without any warning.

Again, so far as this part of district is still under the Chinese jurisdiction, we are perfectly right to sell these books, for there is nothing wrong and the schools in the Settlement are using them. We can not understand for what reason or reasons, that these textbooks should be taken to the Police Station.

As we are one of the three largest publishers in China, we have suffered a great loss directly or indirectly during this wartime. Our printing plant at Hongkew has been occupied by the Japanese since the outbreak of the war. Now, if this Sales Department down the Foochow Road will again be disturbed, then we are bound to close our business. However, we can imagine what the general public will feel at that time.

For these reasons, you are, therefore, requested to instruct the Central Police Office to return us these books immediately and to continue the spirit of co-operation as before in order to cherish a cultural and educational organisation as such in the Settlement.

Thanking you for your prompt execution in advance,
we remain,

Faithfully yours,
The World Book Co., Ltd.,

K.L. Toh
General Manager

作为纳税人，我们必须投诉，此类行为不仅扰乱了我们的业务，也影响了与工部局的整体合作精神。我们要提醒的是，过去我们曾达成默契，如果有书籍不适合当前局势，警务处会通知我们，我们将据此处理。因此，我们一直享有良好的合作关系，未遇任何麻烦。但现在情况突然改变。此次行动没有任何预警。

再者，就该地区而言，既然仍处于中国管辖之下，我们出售这些书籍是完全正当的，因为这些书籍并无不妥，且租界内的学校正在使用它们。我们无法理解这些教科书被带往警察局的原因或理由。

作为中国三大出版商之一，我们在战时遭受了巨大的直接或间接损失。自战争爆发以来，我们在虹口的印刷厂已被日军占领。现在，如果位于福州路的销售部再次受到干扰，我们将被迫停业。然而，我们可以想象届时公众会有何感受。

基于上述原因，特此请求您指示中央捕房立即归还这些书籍，并延续以往的合作精神，以爱护租界内这样的文化教育机构。

提前感谢您迅速执行，

此致
敬礼，

世界书局有限公司，

总经理
杜联齐 (K.L. Toh)

Eighteen years prior to the inauguration of the
Chinese Republic, a war broke out between China and Japan.
China was defeated and the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed.
China suffered heavy losses.

Taiwan was ceded to Japan, as stipulated in the
Treaty of Shinonoseki. Upon learning of this, the
inhabitants of Taiwan became indignant. One Chu San-kung
(丘仙根) was so angry that he promoted a Righteous and
Brave Corps to resist the Japanese. Several tens of
thousands of persons voluntarily joined him in a few days.

President of the Righteous and Brave Corps and to take charge

in Tai-pei into a Presidential Office, and immediately started
the training of troops, the raising of funds and the procuring
of provisions in preparation for a life-and-death struggle
with the Japanese.

Japanese warships arrived and troops were landed.
The Japanese troops headed straight for Keelung (基隆).
Much disturbance was created by them. The inhabitants of
Taiwan would be killed should they put up even a little
resistance. General Wu Kwoh-hwa (吴国华) bravely
attacked the brutal Japanese soldiers and won a great victory.
The Japanese soldiers fled back to their ships.
